name: telar-desktop
//productName: NAMES THE USER-DATA DIRECTORY, not just the window. Electron's app.getName() prefers this over `name`, and app.getPath('userData') is composed from it — so without it this app's state lives in ~/Library/Application Support/telar-desktop, a directory named after the shell package rather than the product. That directory is now TELAR_HOME for a packaged build (main.js), which makes the name a thing people will read.
description: Telar desktop shell with a shared Electron-owned browser host.
author: Facundo Barbera <facundo.barbera@gmail.com>

scripts.//test:desktop:unit: --timeout IS THE ONLY WAY TO MOVE THE CEILING. `[test] timeout` is not a bunfig.toml key — bun ignores unknown keys silently, so a bunfig here would read as configured and do nothing (#414 shipped exactly that for apps/engine). 20 s because these are the Electron-free unit tests but several still spawn real processes — packaging.test.js runs package-desktop.sh and extracts an asar through bunx — and the credential-lifecycle tests poll a real ~750 ms probe. On the shared CI Mac mini that crosses 5 s for a reason that has nothing to do with the code (#458).

extendInfo.//NSAppleEventsUsageDescription: The string macOS shows in the Automation consent dialog when Telar first drives Codex's Computer Use client. Without it the prompt cannot appear and every computer-use call fails silently with -1743.
extendInfo.NSAppleEventsUsageDescription: Telar uses Computer Use to control Mac apps on your behalf — taking screenshots and performing clicks and keystrokes — through Codex's Computer Use client.
extendInfo.//NSCameraUsageDescription: The string macOS shows the FIRST time a page in Telar's browser asks for the camera (systemPreferences.askForMediaAccess). Without it the request is refused before any dialog can appear, and the page reports NotAllowedError as though a person had said no — which is exactly what #422 was: camera and microphone were never offered, not broken.
extendInfo.NSCameraUsageDescription: Telar's built-in browser needs the camera for sites you allow it on — video calls and anything that asks. Telar asks you per site first, and never turns the camera on by itself.
extendInfo.//NSMicrophoneUsageDescription: The microphone half of the same gate. Both strings must be in the packaged Info.plist; a signed build without them denies silently rather than prompting.
extendInfo.NSMicrophoneUsageDescription: Telar's built-in browser needs the microphone for sites you allow it on — calls, dictation and anything that asks. Telar asks you per site first, and never listens by itself.
